# `css/no-unknown-property`

**No unknown properties**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-css` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `ignoreProperties`, `checkPrefixed` |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (the closest known name is a guess at what was meant) |
| **Stability** | `stable` |
| **Since** | 0.1.0 |
| **Ported from** | `stylelint/property-no-unknown` |

## What it checks

Every property is a known CSS property. Custom properties, vendor-prefixed properties and descriptors inside at-rules such as `@font-face` are skipped.

**Why:** The browser drops a declaration whose property it does not know, so a typo silently loses the style.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css
pip install codelaw-rules-css
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css/recommended` sets it to `error`:

```toml
extends = ["codelaw:css/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css/no-unknown-property" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreProperties` | `string[]` | `[]` | properties to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |
| `checkPrefixed` | `boolean` | `false` | also check vendor-prefixed properties |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."css/no-unknown-property"]
severity = "error"

[rules."css/no-unknown-property".options]
ignoreProperties = []
checkPrefixed = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"css/no-unknown-property" = { severity = "error", options = { ignoreProperties = ["<name>"], checkPrefixed = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `ignoreProperties`

*string[]* · default `[]`

properties to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern

```toml
[rules."css/no-unknown-property".options]
ignoreProperties = ["<name>"]
```

#### `checkPrefixed`

*boolean* · default `false`

also check vendor-prefixed properties

```toml
[rules."css/no-unknown-property".options]
checkPrefixed = true
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css/no-unknown-property" = { options = { ignoreProperties = ["<name>"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css/no-unknown-property" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css/no-unknown-property" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css/no-unknown-property" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css/no-unknown-property" = { severity = "warn", options = { ignoreProperties = ["<name>"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css/no-unknown-property": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"ignoreProperties": ["<name>"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-unknown-property: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css/no-unknown-property: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-unknown-property expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css/no-unknown-property --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css/no-unknown-property       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css/no-unknown-property  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>           # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css
a {
  colr: red;
}
```

#### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
a {
  colr: red;
}
```

#### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

## Differences from the source

The property table is `known-css-properties` plus the names stylelint keeps from before it moved to CSSTree, not CSSTree's MDN-derived data. A fix is offered when a known property is one or two edits away.
